name: Monogate
description: Open-source mathematics stack built on the EML operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y). Includes the Pfaffian-cost analyzer (eml-cost) with three prediction functions for SymPy compile-time, float64 numerical precision loss, and PyTorch per-layer activation behavior. Cross-validated against a Lean 4 formalization (monogate-lean, measured 2026-09-12 at 9c6164b): 33 files, 31 of them with no sorry; InfiniteZerosBarrier.lean (2, Part D) and ChainOrderAdditivity.lean (3) carry the 5 documented sorries.

capabilities.name: EML universality
capabilities.description: The single binary operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y) generates every elementary function as a finite tree from the constant 1 alone. Lean-formalized as the IsEMLElementary predicate in Universality.lean. The Lean theorem is the definitional form (IsEMLElementary f implies f is realized by an EML tree); that every elementary function satisfies the predicate is the published result.

capabilities.name: Infinite Zeros Barrier (T01)
capabilities.description: Real EML trees have finitely many zeros on any closed bounded interval where they are real-analytic, while sin(x) has infinitely many. Therefore sin is not an element of EML(R). Parts A, B, C, C-prime are closed in Lean. Part D (sin_not_in_eml, sin_not_in_real_EML_k) carries 2 documented sorries pending o-minimal / Wilkie 1996 machinery not yet in Mathlib.

capabilities.name: SuperBEST v5.3 routing table
capabilities.description: Routing table mapping 10 positive-domain arithmetic operations to F16 expressions, achieving 14n / 80.8% savings vs the 73n naive baseline, plus a general-domain 8-op basket at 16n / 74.2% savings vs the 62n naive baseline. Library, blog, browser, and capability-card surfaces are synchronized from monogate.superbest. Lean (ModelAudit.lean) checks the positive-domain one-node witnesses and the 14n total; the general-domain 16n / 74.2% figures are not Lean-checked.

capabilities.name: SB(add) >= 2
capabilities.description: No single F16 operator equals (x, y) -> x + y for all real x, y. Exhaustive 16-witness refutation in AddLowerBound.lean.

capabilities.name: SB(sub) >= 2
capabilities.description: No single F16 operator equals (x, y) -> x - y for all real x, y. SubLowerBound.lean, 16-case refutation.

capabilities.name: SB(mul) >= 2
capabilities.description: No single F16 operator equals (x, y) -> x * y for all real x, y. MulLowerBound.lean, derivative obstruction route + witness refutation.

capabilities.name: SB(div) >= 2
capabilities.description: No single F16 operator equals (x, y) -> x / y for all real x, y. DivLowerBound.lean.

capabilities.name: estimate_time(expr) compile-time predictor
capabilities.description: Predicts SymPy compile wall-time across simplify/factor/cse/lambdify proxies from the Pfaffian profile. Regression model fit on 202 expressions (cross-domain-3 R v2). 5-fold CV R^2 by proxy: simplify 0.68, factor 0.76, cse 0.83, lambdify 0.84.

capabilities.name: predict_precision_loss(expr) runtime numerical predictor
capabilities.description: Predicts float64 numerical relerr versus 50-digit mpmath ground truth. Fit on 379 expressions from the bench-300-domain corpus. 5-fold CV R^2 = +0.271 +/- 0.060, residual log10 std = 0.772, marginal eml_depth coefficient +0.337 (~0.34 decimal digits per depth unit). Modest signal explicitly NOT used as a form recommender (E-193 Phase 3 best-pick was 30 percent on rewrite tests, below the 70 percent product threshold).

capabilities.name: diagnose(model) per-layer activation behavior (eml-cost-torch)
capabilities.description: Per-layer per-activation lookup of fp16 drift and activation-variance for 19 named PyTorch activation classes. Five seeds per activation, ranked from GeGLU (high drift ~7.4e-4) to Hardsigmoid (low drift ~2.3e-4). The earlier PNE-vs-EML generalization (E-183) was empirically falsified on a controlled corpus (p=0.085); honest_note baked into report.empirical_basis.

capabilities.name: eml-cost CLI
capabilities.description: Console command exposing analyze + estimate_time + predict_precision_loss as `eml-cost report` and `eml-cost check`. Pre-commit usable via --max-simplify-ms and --max-digits-lost budgets. Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 threshold violation, 2 parse error, 64 usage.

capabilities.name: JavaScript port via monogate/cost subpath
capabilities.description: JavaScript port of analyze + predict_precision_loss in npm monogate 1.3.0, with byte-identical Python coefficients. Cost-class fingerprint matches Python eml-cost on 32 of 32 reference cases. predict_precision_loss matches byte-for-byte on 14 of 20 representative cases; remaining 6 differ by up to about a factor of 10 due to SymPy automatic canonicalizations on the JS-parsed literal tree.

capabilities.name: p2-d5-w2-c1 cost-class enrichment in the bench-300-domain corpus
capabilities.description: Across the 403-expression cross-domain corpus and N_null=5000 random expressions, cost class p2-d5-w2-c1 shows 2.7x enrichment with q < 1e-4 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 31 candidate classes, spanning 18 distinct domains. Earlier headline of 'binary 0/50 null with >= 40x enrichment' was a small-N artifact and is corrected here.

capabilities.name: F16 Operator Taxonomy
capabilities.description: Census (Sixteen_Operator_Census.tex) of binary operators formed from exp(±x) and ln(y) with arithmetic, a different sixteen from the F16 on /framework. 16 total: 8 complete, 1 approximate, 7 impossible. A conjecture (catalog T12, T24, T26–T28): the arguments on paper have gaps, the DEML case (T13) and the LEX case (T28) among them, and over the reals the count of 8 complete is false (every real EAL tree is nondecreasing); not formalized in Lean.

capabilities.name: Public Equation Catalog
capabilities.description: 265 named equations across 18+ scientific domains, each annotated with EML decomposition and Pfaffian cost class. Its browsable explorer on monogate.dev was archived on 2026-09-12.

capabilities.name: ELC(ℝ) Characterization
capabilities.description: ELC(ℝ) = closure of ℝ ∪ {1} under eml equals the set of all functions expressible as finite compositions of real exp and ln. Odrzywołek 2026, arXiv:2603.21852. Published proof; not formalized in Lean.

capabilities.name: Euler Gateway (Complex Bridge)
capabilities.description: exp(ix) = cos(x) + i·sin(x) bridges real EML to complex domain, enabling sin/cos construction via Im/Re extraction of eml(ix, 1).

capabilities.name: Cost decomposition (Pfaffian profile)
capabilities.description: The eml-cost analyzer assigns every EML tree a Pfaffian profile (r, mr, d, so) used to predict computational cost and structural complexity; the predictions are validated empirically. Catalog T38, Cost = NaiveCost − SharingDiscount − PatternBonus, is a definition, not a theorem, and none of this is formalized in Lean.

capabilities.name: softplus activation
capabilities.description: softplus(x) = ln(1 + exp(x)) = LEAd(x, 1). Single-node EML expression.

capabilities.name: sigmoid activation
capabilities.description: sigmoid(x) = 1/(1+exp(-x)). DAG cost is the canonical 5n value (shared subexpression); strict tree cost is 6n.

capabilities.name: Adam optimizer (per-param-per-step)
capabilities.description: Adam update with shared bias-correction scalars amortized across parameters. Post-NN-13 re-audit: 31n amortized; strict/tree value is 37n.

capabilities.name: RMSNorm
capabilities.description: RMSNorm(x) = x / sqrt(mean(x²) + ε). EML cost scales with hidden dimension; reported value is for d=4096 (LLM-scale layer).

capabilities.name: eml-stdlib — verified standard library for game development
capabilities.description: v0.4.0 (2026-05-07) ships 178 EML modules / 521 functions / 466 verified across 22 categories: math, signal, control, physics, circuits, sensors, biology (incl. biology/abilities), carriers, quantum, ml, ballistics, plus the 60-module gaming/ family (noise, textures, shading, lighting, terrain, animation, particles, camera, audio, physics). Each module declares chain order and ~89% carry @verify(lean) contracts. Installable via pip; .eml source files ship inside the wheel for downstream Forge tooling. Mirrored as GDScript inside the four Godot prototypes.

capabilities.name: Godot game prototypes (eml-stdlib applied)
capabilities.description: Four Godot 4 prototypes — spellforge (1v1 rune-graph duel; spells are EML expression trees), longshot (2D sniper sim mirroring eml-stdlib::ballistics), apex-predator (asymmetric PvP; hunter has real ballistics, beast has real biology + 4-stage evolution; 25 species, 2v1 split-screen with per-viewport fragment-shader fog of war), monowave (deterministic music visualizer; same audio in → same visuals out, no randomness anywhere). All four ship a CLAUDE.md handoff doc plus a headless smoke-test suite (76 tests total). Private repos under agent-maestro/. The 10 ability kernels first written for apex-predator were promoted to eml-stdlib/biology/abilities/ in stdlib v0.4.

proofs.name: SB(add) >= 2
proofs.statement: No single F16 operator computes x + y for all real x and y.
proofs.proof_method: Witness-based case analysis over all 16 F16 operators; paired with a 2-node upper-bound construction.

proofs.name: SB(sub) >= 2
proofs.statement: No single F16 operator computes x - y for all real x and y.

proofs.name: SB(mul) >= 2
proofs.statement: No single F16 operator computes x * y for all real x and y.

proofs.name: SB(div) >= 2
proofs.statement: No single F16 operator computes x / y for all real x and y.

proofs.name: EML universality witness
proofs.statement: Every EML-elementary function is realized by an EML routing tree.

proofs.name: Infinite Zeros Barrier (T01) — partial
proofs.statement: Real EML trees have finitely many zeros on any closed bounded interval where they are real-analytic. Parts A, B, C, C-prime fully closed; Part D (sin not in EML) carries 2 documented sorries.
proofs.proof_method: Bolzano-Weierstrass + AnalyticOnNhd identity theorem (Parts B and C); Part D requires o-minimal / Wilkie 1996 machinery not yet in Mathlib.
proofs.sorries_description: sin_not_in_eml and sin_not_in_real_EML_k pending a quantitative o-minimal zero-count bound not yet formalized in Mathlib.

proofs.name: Exp–Log Multiplier Duality at Fixed Points
proofs.statement: At any fixed point z of Complex.exp in the slit plane, (exp)′(z)·(log)′(z) = 1.
proofs.proof_method: Chain rule with Mathlib's Complex.hasDerivAt_exp and Complex.hasDerivAt_log; the exp multiplier at the fixed point equals z.

proofs.name: Hyperbolic functions as exp arithmetic
proofs.statement: sinh x = (exp x − exp(−x))/2, cosh x = (exp x + exp(−x))/2 and tanh x = sinh x / cosh x for real x. The ELC-closure consequence is not stated in Lean.
proofs.proof_method: Mathlib identities Real.sinh_eq, Real.cosh_eq and Real.tanh_eq_sinh_div_cosh.

proofs.name: EAL–EXL self-map conjugacy via exp
proofs.statement: For x > 0, exp(exp x)·ln(exp x) = exp(exp x + ln x): the EXL diagonal map is conjugate to the EAL diagonal map through exp, and EDL to EML for x ≠ 1 (under this file's EXL/EDL naming).
proofs.proof_method: Rewriting with Real.exp_add, Real.log_exp and Real.exp_log.

proofs.name: Positive-domain one-node constructions (SuperBEST)
proofs.statement: Seven positive-domain identities, each one F16 node: exp, mul (x, y > 0), pow (x > 0), recip (x > 0), sqrt (x > 0), ln via EXL, and exp(x + ln y) = exp(x)·y (y > 0). The 14n positive-domain total is summed in ModelAudit.lean (superbest_v53_positive_total).
proofs.proof_method: Mathlib rewrites: Real.exp_add, Real.exp_log, Real.rpow_def_of_pos, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow.

verification.lean_original_eml_theorems_note: Hand classification from the 2026-04-26 audit (monogate-research data/lean.md; excludes Mathlib wrappers and sorry-stubs). It has not been re-derived since those files changed, and no check verifies it.
verification.evidence_summary: Lean (measured 2026-09-12 at monogate-lean 9c6164b): 31 of 33 files contain no sorry; InfiniteZerosBarrier.lean (2, Part D) and ChainOrderAdditivity.lean (3) carry the 5 documented sorries. `lake build` succeeds, and every lean_theorem named in this card is re-checked before each deploy (compiled at a pinned commit, #print axioms read; scripts/lean_claims.json). Test counts are as of last_verified (2026-05-25) and are not re-run by that gate.

honest_limitations: predict_precision_loss is NOT a form recommender; cost class does not reliably pick the more numerically stable form within an algebraic equivalence class (E-193 Phase 3 best-pick = 30 percent across 10 rewrite tests).

Form-sensitivity: about 50 percent of textbook expressions yield different cost classes for algebraically equivalent forms. canonicalize() preprocessing reduces this to about 35 percent. The remaining drift is documented.

Real-world (bio / physics / engineering) expressions are NOT specially numerically clean compared to random nulls at matched cost class (pooled diff = -0.001 log10 across 4 matched classes; E-193 Phase 4).
diagnose(model) per-activation drift values are measured on a single fixed FFN; per-architecture variation is not yet characterized.
JS port of predict_precision_loss matches Python byte-for-byte on 14 of 20 representative cases; 6 of 20 differ by up to about a factor of 10 due to SymPy automatic canonicalization differences.
